title: Deal-saver scripts: model fallbacks & cost anchors for field
content:
Summary:

This is a compact, field-focused battlecard intended for AE/SEs to rescue at-risk deals where customers compare Redwood Inference to generic LLM API providers. Focus: pragmatic scripts (what to say), concrete evidence (what to show quickly), and escalation triggers (when to involve Solutions Eng). Not a product spec — tactical messaging that closes stalls related to cost, latency/SLOs, and enterprise controls.

Why this exists (use cases):
- Customer: running a pilot where per-token bills are spiking on broad query sets.
- Customer: worried about reliability when traffic bursts (internal incident in competitor logs).
- Customer: needs private deployment for compliance but fears the migration lift.

Top 3 field claims (short, repeatable):
1) Predictable economics: "We give you levers that change unit cost without changing model quality — batching, cache, and quantization profiles are measurable and reversible."
2) Reliability-first serving: "We route, fallback, and surface degradations before the app does — minimizing outages and noisy failures."
3) Same interface everywhere: "Hosted, Dedicated, Private — same API & rollout controls so you can test hosted then lift-and-shift with minimal rewrites."

Quick evidence to surface in a demo (under 6 minutes):
- Cost anchor: bring a 1-page cost delta snapshot (sample workload) — show tokens/second, expected monthly cost with/without batching and with a quantized variant.
- Latency SLO: show a per-route latency dashboard for a synthetic burst (50 concurrent sessions) and call out the fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant that preserved p95.
- Security: highlight an audit log row + KMS integration screenshot for VPC/private deployment checklist.

Common competitive traps and short rebuttals (one-liners + follow-up asks):
Trap: "They give cheaper per-token pricing today."
Rebuttal: "Long-term unit economics are what matter. Tell me which metric keeps you up at night — cost per completed user action or raw token cost?"
Follow-up: request a sample request mix and offer to run a 48-hour cost projection with suggested batching/cache settings.

Trap: "Their SLA is higher / they advertised 99.99%."
Rebuttal: "SLA numbers only matter if they translate into routing and fallback policy behavior under stress. Show me an example scenario you fear and I’ll map our fallback & rollback plan to it in 24 hours."

Trap: "Migration to private infra is risky/expensive."
Rebuttal: "We decouple control-plane and runtime; customers typically do a phased private rollout with our lift-and-shift template and we own the first deployment with you."

Objection handling scripts (word-for-word options):
- Cost objection (concerned about token cost):
  AE Script: "Totally valid — most pilots under-index on cache/batching. If you share 2–3 representative prompts, we’ll run a quick fuzz run and show realistic cost with our suggestions. If it doesn't look better, you walk."
  SE Add-on: "We can demo token-level breakdown in 15 minutes and produce a saved config (batch size + cache TTL + quantization candidate) you can test in staging."

- Reliability objection (fear of outages):
  AE Script: "I hear you — downtime = revenue risk. We instrument per-route SLOs, automatic regional fallback, and model-level graceful degradation. Let me sketch the fallback chain for your critical route now."
  SE Add-on: "We'll run a chaos test against your staging traffic shape and share the incident playbook we apply for similar customers."

- Compliance objection (private data):
  AE Script: "We can start hosted with data protections, and execute a clear migration path to a Private control plane or on-prem. We have templates for KMS/HSM and audit logging."
  SE Add-on: "We'll put together a minimal network diagram and runbook — turnkey for our first customer session."

Tactical play: the 3-step "Deal-saver" rescue call (15–30 minutes)
1) Re-anchor metrics (5 mins): AE asks the buyer for the top 2 metrics (cost per interaction, p95 latency, or TTR). Record and validate.
2) Rapid demo/proof (8–12 mins): SE runs a pre-built script — show cost delta for provided sample (batching ON/OFF), show a live fallback (simulate a model instance drop), and display audit log/KMS row.
3) Commit to an immediate action (2–3 mins): either a 48-hour trial with a guarded config or a joint technical plan for private pilot. Capture next steps and assign SE/AE owners.

Show-and-tell assets to keep handy (one-liners + file names):
- 48hr-cost-projection-template.csv — input: sample traffic, outputs: projected monthly spend w/variants.
- quick-fallback-demo.postman — simulates model failure and shows auto-routing.
- private-deploy-mini-runbook.pdf — 6-step checklist for first private deployment run.
- route-slo-screenshot.png — annotated p95/p99 dashboard you can share in calls.

When to escalate to Solutions Engineering / Customer Success:
- Customer asks for a live, production-grade private deployment within 14 days -> Escalate immediately.
- Customer insists on sub-50ms p95 across the globe for custom LLM -> Escalate — requires infra planning.
- Customer will sign only with a paid migration service or ramped SLA -> Escalate and involve CS for contract/ops design.

Red flags that signal a losing deal (call these out early):
- Customer evaluates solely on raw per-token price and refuses to share a sample workload.
- Customer asks for an unbounded discount before we can show measurable unit economics improvements.
- Customer expects to replicate hyper-specific latency targets without producing traffic shape or acceptance tests.

Field tips (small repeats that win):
- Always offer to "run the numbers" — framing the conversation around their workload shifts discussion from list price to unit economics.
- Keep a quantization anecdote ready: "For X workload, 8-bit quantization reduced GPU costs by ~30% with <2% quality delta in our evals."
- Use the fallback demo as a human-safe demo: demonstrating a failed instance and graceful routing builds trust faster than slides.

Short templates for follow-up emails (pick and paste)
- Post-call: "Thanks — per our call, I’ve attached the 48hr cost template and the quick-fallback demo. We’ll run your sample through tonight and share results tomorrow EOD. — Sofia"
- Trial offer: "We’ll spin a guarded trial for 48 hours: fixed budget cap, preconfigured batching+cache, and a rollback policy. If it meets your cost & latency goals, we’ll scope next steps. — AE name"

Appendix: Suggested internal checklist for a rescue run (single-line items for a quick read):
- Confirm sample workload exists and is accessible.
- Prepare cost projection CSV + two quantization candidates.
- Pre-stage a fallback route and test postman script.
- Prepare a one-slide diagram of private deployment lift (network & KMS).
- Assign SE for live demo and note escalation triggers.

Notes / working questions (things we should iterate on in the doc):
- Create an automated tool to ingest sample requests and produce the cost projection CSV in <1 hour.
- Collect 3 anonymized case studies where caching/batching reduced pilot costs by >25%.
- Add a short video walkthrough of the fallback demo for AE enablement.

End of doc.
